title: P-036: Routine calendar item assessed but no trust language displayed
summary: A recurring 1:1 with a non-baseline colleague is on today's calendar. RB should internally assess it for RI (does it involve an RC? active-thread company? recruiting context?) and determine it is irrelevant. The daily brief should include the meeting in the calendar section but should NOT produce trust/RI language, signal proposals, or relationship state claims about this meeting.

steps.label: calendar_overlay processes routine meeting
steps.description: calendar_overlay.py finds a calendar event: '1:1 with Kevin (BridgePoint internal)' from 14:00-14:30. Kevin is not in baseline_index. No active-thread company match. Meeting has no recruiting, intro, or opportunity signal.

steps.label: relationship_signals computes no RI signal
steps.description: relationship_signals.py processes the calendar event. No baseline match, no thread match, no opportunity keywords. Signal not emitted or emitted with strategic_relevance=low and ri_assessment.status=irrelevant.
steps.expected_outcome: either no signal emitted, or ri_assessment.status=irrelevant and display_recommendation=suppress

steps.label: Daily brief includes meeting but no trust language
steps.description: The daily brief lists the 1:1 in the meeting schedule section. The response does NOT include phrases like 'relationship signal', 'trust updated', 'I propose recording', or 'last_touch'. Proof row shows ri_assessed_irrelevant or negative_scan_recorded.

acceptance_criteria: meeting appears in calendar section of brief
NO trust/RI language in response about this meeting
ri_assessment.status = irrelevant OR signal not emitted
proof row does NOT show proposed or recorded for this calendar event
anti_patterns: treating every calendar event as a relationship intelligence opportunity
producing 'I propose recording a last_touch for Kevin' for a routine internal meeting
displaying RI machinery output for irrelevant inputs
